`make_jira_issue_tracker <- function(issues) {

  issue_tracker <- list()

  # combine the issues into a list
  issues <- list(issue1, issue2)
  issue_tracker[["base_info"]] <- lapply(issues,"[[", "base_info")
  issue_tracker[["ext_info"]] <- lapply(issues, "[[", "ext_info")

  folder_path <- "~/Desktop"
  jira_json_path <- file.path(folder_path,"fake_issue_tracker.json")
  jsonlite::write_json(issue_tracker,file.path(folder_path,"fake_issue_tracker.json"))

  issue_tracker <- list(base_info = list(), ext_info = list())

  return(jira_json_path)

}`

I don't think it should be detrimental, but I thought that I should note it. (In hindsight, this is probably just related to me not getting or pathing the dependencies correctly)

### devtools::test()
 #263 devtools::test() returned several failures and after receiving help through the discussions tab and installing third-party dependencies, I was able to fix most of them. 

Perhaps more descriptive error messages such as “this failed because you did not install tool x” would be helpful. Many of the failures were fixed after installing third party apps, though the response in the discussion tab was helpful.

### missing functions in kaiaulu_architecture.rmd
#271 As a new user to Rstudio, I had assumed that the missing functions were defined in another file in the project similar to a webdev app. I found that I was missing packages after some googling. I also looked at the require methods on the top, which indicated some missing requirements, though this was only an 'alright' indicator as the requirements shared some similarities with the function names but were not identical. Eg. "missing funcition: visIgraph" was in the package "visNetwork"

### Perceval Install
- Instalingl the third party tools: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/wiki/Third-Party-Tools-Setup
One note is that the instruction for installing perceval did not work as described on the third party tools tab. Changing the ‘=’ to ‘==’ fixed the problem and perceval was installed without a hitch. I am using the Terminal on a Mac so I am not sure if this is a unique distinction for my situation. 

pip3 install perceval=0.12.24  should be pip3 install perceval==0.12.24 

I didn’t have any issues with the other third party tools, though.

### difficulty downloading data
https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/discussions/264#discussion-6133995
I had difficulty downloading data. First, the file structure was difficult to figure out. The default for most downloads was something like ../../rawdata/ and it was confusing which directory I was currently working in. The file browser in Rstudio would be in one file and the getwd() command would show that I was working in a different file, so I changed the filepaths in the config files manually to something like ~/CAPTSTONE496/rawdata/something so I wouldn't even have to think about my working directory. 

The data also didn't download when I pressed "run all". Running each chunk one at a time initiated the download process, though the process took a long time to download the files. I think that there could be a message saying "download in process. This may take a while depending on how many issues are extracted" or something like that.  The docs could also maybe advise running each chunk one at a time and/or warn that downloads may take some time. 

### line_metric_showcase.rmd
https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/discussions/273#discussion-6165072
Line 93 had an error due to the scc path. The third party tools on the wiki links to the release version and prompts you to download it. I had downloaded the source code file instead of the proper file and resulted in not having a binary in that file to path to. Perhaps a note to explicitly not download the source file would be useful.

- [x] #266 This issue was due to incorrect paths of perceval and git_repo_path. At first, I thought that the "rawdata" folder would be automatically created when I ran the program but I later found out that I had to create that folder myself. I also found it hard to understand the ".." folder that was default in all of the config files. I found it much easier to replace the default path entirely with my own file path that did not use "..".

- [x] #267 I was unaware of the "ls -a" command that showed the hidden folders. I also did not know that I had to create the token file myself and paste my token in that file. 

- [x] #270 I had errors with downloading igraph for my system. When I tried to run install.packages("igraph"), it would give me an error that I do not remember. So, I looked online and found a stack overflow forum explaining how to download igraph with the console. 

- [x] #272 This issue is similar to #266 because I did not understand the ".." folder in the config files. After I had changed the default paths to direct paths and creating the missing folders, the issues were solved.

- [x] #274 I did not know that I had to download a .mbox file before running this vignette. I tried running the download_mod_mbox.Rmd to download .mbox files but they were not the correct files. I later found in the geronimo config file that there was a link for the geronimo mailbox where I could download it there.

Notes:

- Use this httr version: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/9294a9bb92506b76424b0fcc7c07f6b74d5ce53d/DESCRIPTION#L39
- Get used to JIRA as an issue tracker using Kaiaulu JIRA Sandbox: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/252 
- Try to use the Existing Download JIRA Notebook to download said data. You want to understand how the data you see downloaded relates to the data in the web interface. In addition, consider the data the JirAgileR library offers via Kaiaulu Notebook. You want to ensure you obtain minimally the same data and columns.
- Make sure you understand how **pagination** works. 
- Want to make sure you use the appropriate API Endpoint in order to enable Refresh, so issue https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/253 is addressed.
- For information on JIRA API and how it all works, with examples so you try on a browser, see: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/228 

- You want to iterate early with me both in discussion and code so I can provide early feedback before you go too far. Follow the guidelines to send a PR here: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md 
- Also, have a look on how to organize your Issue (in particular the first post, so it is easier for everyone to refer to):https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/master/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/student.md 
- Let's adopt Code revision discussion = PR. Issue clarifications = Issue. Separating is more accessible as the various code revisions can make finding information of the issue harder. 

I may edit this message to add more information if needed unless I am replying to a subsequent comment. In that case, no e-mail will be sent as a notification.
Edit: Moved issue description to the top post.

As mentioned previously, I was wondering if I am supposed to be redoing that fake data generator with a new API or am I expanding on what they have done already? I wrote down that we were using the HTTR api but I forget if that was for the other parts of the milestone.

I would not call for an extension but rather a replacement. The basic issue is https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/228. Here's why we need to replace: We are currently relying on JirAgileR to download the issue data. The Fake Data Generator that tests the parser function is therefore dependent on JirAgileR. 

Unfortunately, this package modifies the raw data one would obtain from the issue tracker. The Fake JIRA Issue Generator for the issue tracker, therefore, ended up dependent on a data format of JirAgileR, instead of JIRA. Since we are replacing JirAgileR by our own crawler, we should also adjust the JIRA Fake Issue Data Generator accordingly. 

You should be able to reuse most of the existing code, but there are some fixes and improvements that should be made.

Also important to keep in mind: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/258

See: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/228

You will also want to start practicing the parser using Kaiaulu's JIRA Sandbox.

I have written a new function that downloads the data based on the fields required. There are separate function calls to acquire the issue data and the comment data along the search api. I have recently implemented pagination: 

https://github.com/Ssunoo2/kaiaulu/blob/a0b18712865a2e29605c09424f2f987f1ba27eb0/vignettes/Download_jira_data_without_JirAgileR_pagination_newfilesforeach.Rmd#L133-L144

The pagination works by constructing a new filename along the path designated in the config file. Currently it appends the issue id and the time downloaded, though these are subject to change in the future, especially if they become pivotal in implementing a refresh capability. 

I am experimenting with ways to implement a refresh capability. My main lack of understanding right now is what field I should be checking, though I am leaning towards the "created" field so that I only download issues created after the most recent created date that exists in the files already downloaded. I was also toying with the idea of using the issue id field, though I'm not completely sure how these numbers are created, as for instance in the geronimo issues, there are ids between 0 and 782, then seemingly out of place issues 2665, 4273, 5184, etc, and I am unsure if they are necessarily correlated to their created date (eg larger ids are more recently created). If they are, then I can do a check for the largest issue id and then write something that only downloads ids larger than the current largest. I am referencing the information in #228 to help guide me.

Before, with the original downloader, the issues downloaded with comments and issues downloaded without comments were all together in their respective json files, and those json files could be easily pointed to by just putting in their respective pathway into the parser function. Now with Sean’s downloader, they’re all out in the same directory. Since I have to iterate over each file to parse them individually, there’s a possibility that my function will just iterate through all of the json files indiscriminately, parsing both the comment and comment-less issues at the same time.

I have two proposals to prevent this from happening:
1. Create two separate folders in the usual pathway to house the comment and comment-less json files separately. The way I see it, it works similarly to how the original downloader saved the json files for each issue. The new folders represents the original json files that the issue data resides in, and the data in this case would be the new json files that Sean’s downloader creates.
2. Create an extra parameter in my parser function that dictates whether to parse the issue_comments json files or the comment-less json files. It’d be something like parse_jira(path, a). For example, should parameter “a” be a string “comment”, then the function will only read the json files that were created with a comments field.

@ian-lastname Iterating over the set of files you wish for can be done with the `list.files` function in a directory. This will give you the list of filepaths as a character vector. You can then use stringi library to pattern match the elements of the character vector which file name are used for comments (you have to have different file name conventions for those with and without comments).

However, before you pursue this, I strongly advise you to do what I recommended and edit post 1 using the proposed change template. Without that, I can't assess what functions you are trying to write. We may need to re-do again at the end of the week if it does not match what it should be. >  add a username/password setting to a config file. The password is an Atlassian token

>  The new downloader function removes the downloading of extraneous data  

I believe you are referring to baseinfo and extinfo here? If so, then this is not quite accurate. This is not additional data downloaded by JirAgileR, it is downloading the issue data as we are from the endpoint, but it adds additional metadata offline. This just adds overhead and forces unit tests on our end to comply to its interface rather than the issue tracker. That's why we want to get away from it. 

> The purpose of eventual pagination is the future implementation of a refresh capability in which only issues that have not already been downloaded can be downloaded again. 

This is not accurate. Pagination is its own separate thing than the refresh capability we also want to add. Pagination just means you are not just downloading the first page worth of issues, but iterate through multiple pages. You can have pagination without the refresh capability. But this is inefficient: Every time you run the function, it downloads everything again. The problem is introduced is reflected on https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/253 for GitHub which has an API key, but I can imagine for very large JIRA projects, an IP block would be issued if it just tried to download everything in one go. This is why the refresh is so important: So the data can be downloaded in chunks. 

I will also add that the downloader should be able to request information from the parser to know the time range (and/or issue range) to download the new issues accordingly. The parser will not provide the downloader with a page number: This would introduce duplicates. There is a [website](https://www.lexjansen.com/pharmasug-cn/2021/SR/Pharmasug-China-2021-SR031.pdf) I found that shows that jsonlite puts vectors of length 1 into arrays of length 1. In order to solve this issue, when I call write_json, I set the auto_unbox parameter to TRUE. 

For example: 
`jsonlite::write_json(rtn_json_issues, save_filepath, auto_unbox = TRUE)`

auto_unbox automatically "unboxes" all atomic vectors of length 1 and makes it a key-value pair. This way, the written JSON file will have the exact same format as a JSON file from an API call.

I identified an issue in the refresher that results in duplicate issues being downloaded. Because the format of the API request is YYYY-MM-DD, if you were to identify 2020-01-01 as the most recent value of the created field and then appended ‘AND created >= 2020-01-01’ to the api request, you would download the issues created on that date again. Conversely, if you were to use ‘>’ rather than ‘>=’, you may skip any files that were created on 2020-01-01 but at a later time than the ‘most recent issue’. For this reason, I will adapt the function to to use issuekeys instead.

The parser created in #276 previously returned a date of the most recently created file in a filepath. It will now be altered to return the filename that holds the most recent issue. A new wrapper function will be created that will open this file and return the greatest issueKey value and append it to the JQL query so that only issues greater than this key will be downloaded. This should solve the issue of duplicate files being downloaded.
